root_cause.text: The netem_enqueue() function in sch_netem.c uses `skb_headlen(skb)` as the ceiling for a random index without checking if it is zero, so when a fully non-linear packet (headlen==0) is processed, `get_random_u32_below(0)` returns an unconstrained 32-bit value causing an out-of-bounds write to `skb->data`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (skb_headlen(skb))` before the corruption line, and the commit message explains that `get_random_u32_below(0)` returns an unconstrained random integer, leading to out-of-bounds access when used as an offset.
